subject: Financial Accounting
notes: Comma-free fields for safe paste-CSV import. Numerical answers are stated in the correctAnswer field with the working shown in explanation.

questions.text: The process of recording business transactions in the books of accounts is called
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Book keeping is the systematic recording of financial transactions.

questions.text: Which accounting principle says revenue should be recorded when it is earned not when cash is received
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: The accrual concept records revenue and expenses when they occur regardless of cash flow.

questions.text: The accounting equation is expressed as Assets equals Liabilities plus
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Assets equal liabilities plus owners equity or capital.

questions.text: The convention of conservatism means anticipate no profit but provide for all possible losses
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Conservatism guides accountants to be cautious and not overstate income or assets.

questions.text: State any four users of accounting information
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.correctAnswer: Owners investors creditors managers government and employees.
questions.explanation: Each user needs accounting information for different decisions.

questions.text: Explain the going concern concept and its significance
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.correctAnswer: The going concern concept assumes the business will continue for the foreseeable future. Assets are therefore valued at cost and not at liquidation value and expenses are allocated over periods.
questions.explanation: This assumption underlies depreciation and the classification of assets and liabilities.

questions.text: A business has total assets of 500000 and liabilities of 200000. The capital of the owner is
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Capital equals assets minus liabilities so 500000 minus 200000 equals 300000.

questions.text: Which book is the first and original record where transactions are first entered
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: The journal is the book of original entry where transactions are first recorded.

questions.text: The account that is debited when goods are purchased for cash is
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Purchases are debited and cash is credited when goods are bought for cash.

questions.text: The golden rule for personal accounts is debit the receiver and credit the
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Personal accounts follow the rule debit the receiver credit the giver.

questions.text: A trial balance is a statement that verifies the arithmetical accuracy of ledger balances
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: A trial balance checks that total debits equal total credits.

questions.text: Pass the journal entry for goods sold on credit to Ravi for 10000
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.correctAnswer: Debit Ravi account 10000 and credit Sales account 10000.
questions.explanation: Ravi is the receiver so he is debited and sales is a nominal gain so it is credited.

questions.text: Explain the objectives of preparing a trial balance
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.correctAnswer: A trial balance checks arithmetical accuracy of postings and helps locate errors. It provides the balances needed to prepare final accounts and gives a summary of all ledger accounts.
questions.explanation: Note that a tallied trial balance does not guarantee that no errors exist.

questions.text: A firm purchased goods for 25000 and paid carriage of 1000 in cash. The total amount to be debited to purchases is
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Carriage inward is debited separately to carriage account not to purchases unless the question specifies otherwise.

questions.text: The cash book which has both cash and bank columns on each side is called a
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: A two column cash book records cash and bank transactions side by side.

questions.text: Credit sales are recorded in which subsidiary book
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Credit sales go in the sales book while cash sales go in the cash book.

questions.text: The petty cash book is maintained under which system
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Under the imprest system a fixed amount is given to the petty cashier and reimbursed periodically.

questions.text: Cash sales of 5000 should be entered in the sales book
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Only credit sales go in the sales book; cash sales are recorded in the cash book.

questions.text: Distinguish between a cash book and a pass book
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.correctAnswer: A cash book is maintained by the business and records its own cash and bank dealings. A pass book is kept by the bank and shows the same transactions from the banks point of view.
questions.explanation: The same transaction appears on opposite sides of the two books.

questions.text: Explain the advantages of maintaining subsidiary books
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.correctAnswer: Subsidiary books divide the journal so similar transactions are recorded together. They save time allow division of work and make information easy to find and post to the ledger.
questions.explanation: Cover division of work specialisation and ease of posting.

questions.text: A trader received cash 6000 and allowed discount 200. The amount debited to discount allowed is
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Discount allowed is a loss to the business and is debited at the amount of the discount given.

questions.text: A bank reconciliation statement is prepared mainly to
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
options: Reconcile the cash book and pass book balances
questions.explanation: A BRS explains the difference between the bank balance in the cash book and the pass book.

questions.text: Cheques issued but not yet presented for payment cause the cash book balance to be
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Such cheques are already reduced in the cash book but not yet in the pass book so the cash book balance is lower.

questions.text: Bank charges debited by the bank appear only in the pass book and reduce the balance
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Bank charges are recorded by the bank first and lower the pass book balance until entered in the cash book.

questions.text: List any four causes of difference between the cash book and pass book balances
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.correctAnswer: Cheques issued but not presented cheques deposited but not credited bank charges and interest allowed by the bank are common causes.
questions.explanation: Timing differences and bank entries unknown to the business cause the gap.

questions.text: Explain the need for preparing a bank reconciliation statement
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.correctAnswer: A BRS reconciles the two balances so errors and fraud can be detected and delayed items identified. It gives the true bank balance and helps in cash management.
questions.explanation: Cover detection of errors prevention of fraud and correct cash position.

questions.text: The cash book shows a bank balance of 8000. A cheque of 2000 issued is not yet presented. The balance as per pass book will be
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: An unpresented cheque means the pass book still shows the amount so add 2000 to 8000 giving 10000.

questions.text: The final account that shows the financial position of a business on a date is the
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: The balance sheet is a statement of assets and liabilities on a particular date.

questions.text: Closing stock appears in which accounts of the final statements
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Closing stock is credited to the trading account and shown as a current asset in the balance sheet.

questions.text: Outstanding expenses are shown in the balance sheet as a
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Outstanding expenses are amounts due but unpaid so they are a current liability.

questions.text: Carriage inward is shown on the debit side of the trading account
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Carriage inward is a direct expense on purchases so it is debited to the trading account.

questions.text: Explain the difference between capital expenditure and revenue expenditure
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.correctAnswer: Capital expenditure gives benefit over many years and is shown as an asset. Revenue expenditure benefits only the current period and is charged to the profit and loss account.
questions.explanation: The distinction rests on the period of benefit derived from the spending.

questions.text: Describe the adjustments required before preparing final accounts
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.correctAnswer: Key adjustments include closing stock outstanding and prepaid expenses accrued and unearned income depreciation bad debts and provision for doubtful debts. Each adjustment has a dual effect on trading P and L and the balance sheet.
questions.explanation: Explain the dual aspect of each adjustment with its placement.

questions.text: Gross profit is 40000 and operating expenses are 15000. The net profit is
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Net profit equals gross profit minus operating expenses so 40000 minus 15000 equals 25000.

questions.text: The amount charged to the profit and loss account each year for the use of a fixed asset is called
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Depreciation allocates the cost of a fixed asset over its useful life.

questions.text: Under the straight line method depreciation is calculated on the
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Straight line depreciation charges a fixed percentage on the original cost each year.

questions.text: The written down value method of depreciation charges a higher amount in the early years
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: The WDV method applies a fixed rate to the reducing balance so depreciation is higher in early years.

questions.text: The system of accounting that ignores the double entry principle and keeps incomplete records is called
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Single entry keeps only personal and cash accounts and no complete double entry record.

questions.text: State the methods of calculating depreciation
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.correctAnswer: The main methods are straight line method written down value method and annuity and machine hour methods.
questions.explanation: Straight line and WDV are the two most common methods.

questions.text: Explain the causes of depreciation of fixed assets
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.correctAnswer: Depreciation arises from wear and tear from use passage of time obsolescence due to new technology and depletion of natural resources. It matches the cost of the asset with the revenue it earns.
questions.explanation: Cover physical deterioration obsolescence and the matching principle.

questions.text: A machine costs 100000 with scrap value 10000 and useful life ten years. Annual depreciation under straight line method is
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Depreciation equals cost minus scrap divided by life so 90000 divided by 10 equals 9000.

questions.text: Which account is credited when a cheque received from a customer is deposited in the bank
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: The customer account is credited and the bank account is debited when a cheque is banked.

questions.text: Assertion: A trial balance that agrees is proof that no errors exist. Reason: Some errors do not affect the equality of debits and credits
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.topic: Journal Ledger and Trial Balance (assertion reason)
options: Assertion is false but reason is true
Both assertion and reason are true and reason explains assertion
Both are true but reason does not explain assertion
Assertion is true but reason is false
questions.explanation: Errors of omission and compensating errors do not disturb the trial balance so a tallied trial balance is not conclusive proof.

questions.text: Match the book to its content
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: The sales book records credit sales while the cash book records cash transactions.

questions.text: Read the case: A firm paid 12000 as insurance premium for the year. Only 3000 relates to the current period. Identify the amount to be charged to the profit and loss account and the amount to be shown as an asset
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.correctAnswer: 3000 is charged to the profit and loss account as insurance expense and 9000 is shown as prepaid insurance under current assets.
questions.explanation: Only the current years portion is an expense and the balance is prepaid.

questions.text: Read the case: The cash book shows an overdraft of 5000. A cheque of 1500 deposited is not yet credited by the bank. Calculate the balance as per the pass book and state whether it is an overdraft
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.correctAnswer: The pass book shows a larger overdraft of 6500. Since the deposit is not credited by the bank the pass book overdraft is 5000 plus 1500 which equals 6500.
questions.explanation: An uncredited deposit increases the overdraft balance in the pass book.

questions.text: A business bought goods worth 40000 with a trade discount of ten percent. The amount to be recorded in the purchases book is
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Trade discount is deducted before recording so 40000 minus ten percent equals 36000.

questions.text: The balance of the trading account that shows excess of expenses over income from operations is a gross
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: When the debit side of the trading account exceeds the credit side the result is a gross loss.

questions.text: Bad debts written off are shown in the profit and loss account as a loss
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.explanation: Bad debts are irrecoverable amounts and are treated as a loss in the profit and loss account.

questions.text: Explain the limitations of single entry system of accounting
questions.subject: Financial Accounting
questions.correctAnswer: Single entry does not provide a complete double entry record so a true and fair view is not possible. A trial balance cannot be prepared and errors and fraud are hard to detect. It is difficult to value assets and compute accurate profit.
questions.explanation: Cover absence of trial balance difficulty of detection and unreliable profit figures.
